# `connector/enrich/pdf/testdata/`

Fixtures used by the build-tag-gated tests in `../pdf_test.go`
(`//go:build enrichruntime`). The tests only run when the
`enrichruntime` build tag is set AND `pdftotext` is present in PATH —
i.e. inside the `glovebox-enricher-runtime` image (or any local dev
environment with `poppler-utils` installed).

## Files

| File | Size | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `text.pdf` | ~615 B | Single-page PDF whose content stream draws the string `Hello, glovebox PDF enricher test.` — `pdftotext` extracts that line cleanly. |
| `image-only.pdf` | ~436 B | Single-page PDF with an empty content stream (no Text operators). `pdftotext` returns exit 0 with no extractable text. Validates the "tried, found nothing — not a failure" semantic. |
| `encrypted.pdf` | ~905 B | Minimal PDF carrying a Standard-security-handler `/Encrypt` dictionary in the trailer. `pdftotext` rejects with exit 1 and `Command Line Error: Incorrect password`. Validates the encrypted-PDF error classification. |
| `corrupt.pdf` | 41 B | Truncated bytes — a `%PDF-1.4` header followed by the start of an object dictionary, no xref / no trailer / no `%%EOF`. `pdftotext` returns exit 1 with `Syntax Error: End of file inside dictionary`. Validates that we surface a WHAT/CHECK/FIX error without panicking. |

## Provenance

All four fixtures are generated by `gen_fixtures.py` in this directory.
They are hand-rolled PDF 1.4 documents using plain ASCII byte
sequences — no external library dependency, no compression, no images,
no embedded fonts beyond the standard Type1 references. This keeps the
fixtures tiny, reviewable in a diff, and stable against any future
poppler-utils upgrade.

To regenerate:

```
cd connector/enrich/pdf/testdata
python3 gen_fixtures.py
```

The output is byte-deterministic — re-running the generator produces
the same bytes on every host, so `git diff` after a regen should be
empty unless the generator script itself was edited.

## Why these fixtures (and not, e.g., a real-world sample)

A real PDF would either be tiny-but-unreadable (no extractable text,
defeating `TestEnrich_TextPDF`) or larger than necessary and
licensing-encumbered. Hand-rolled gives us:

- predictable behavior across poppler versions
- ~2 KB total committed bytes
- a generator anyone can read to understand what each file exercises

The trade-off: these are not "in the wild" PDFs. The end-to-end smoke
script (`scripts/smoke-enrichment.sh`, future work) is where we'd plug
in a richer fixture archive.
